question: What are the four main vital signs we check for every patient?

options.A: Weight, height, blood glucose, and urine output
options.B: Pain scale, level of consciousness, and skin color
options.C: Temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure
options.D: Muscle strength, reflex response, and pupil size

explanation: Spot on! Temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure are your core vital signs. They give you a quick snapshot of how well a patient's body is functioning. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why do nurses take a baseline set of vital signs when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To diagnose the specific underlying disease condition immediately
options.B: To spot any future changes or signs that the patient is getting worse
options.C: To calculate the exact date of discharge from the hospital
options.D: To determine the correct financial billing category for the ward

explanation: Think of the baseline as your starting point. Having these initial numbers lets you easily notice if your patient starts to deteriorate later on. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which temperature route gives us the truest estimate of the body's core temperature?
explanation: You got it! Because it is enclosed inside the body, the rectal route gives the closest measurement to actual core body temperature. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h2)

question: What can cause a false or inaccurate reading when taking an oral temperature?

options.A: Positioning the patient in a flat supine posture
options.B: Recent ingestion of hot or cold fluids
options.C: Wearing tight clothing around the neck area
options.D: Using a mercury thermometer instead of a digital one

explanation: Hot tea or cold water right before a check will temporarily heat up or cool down the mouth, giving you a false reading. Always wait a few minutes if they just ate or drank! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h2)

question: What physical heart action actually creates the pulse wave you feel at the wrist?

options.C: Opening of the aortic valve leaflets

explanation: When the left ventricle squeezes, it forces a wave of blood out into the arteries. That wave is the pulse you feel under your fingers! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h3)

question: When checking a pulse, what does the term 'pulse character' tell you?

options.A: The regularity of the time intervals between beats
options.B: The exact number of heartbeats counted per minute
options.C: The volume and tension of the arterial pulse wave
options.D: The specific anatomical site used for palpation

explanation: Pulse character is all about the strength and fullness of each beat—whether it feels bounding, strong, weak, or thready. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why do nurses often count a patient's breathing rate right after checking their pulse, without moving their hand away?

options.A: To prevent the patient from consciously altering their breathing rate
options.B: To save time during a busy clinical ward round routine
options.C: To ensure the blood pressure cuff remains properly inflated
options.D: To accurately compare pulse strength against chest wall expansion

explanation: People naturally change how they breathe the moment they know you are watching. By pretending to still take the pulse, you get a true, natural respiration count! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: What term is used when a patient's breathing rate drops dangerously low?
explanation: Brdy- means slow, and pnea means breathing. So bradypnea is a breathing rate that has dropped below the normal range. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if the cuff you use is too narrow for the patient's arm?

options.A: The Korotkoff sounds will completely disappear
options.B: The systolic and diastolic values will remain accurate
options.C: The recorded blood pressure will be falsely low
options.D: The recorded blood pressure will be falsely high

explanation: A narrow cuff takes extra force to squeeze the large arm, which gives you a fake high reading. Always match your cuff size to the patient! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: What does the diastolic blood pressure number represent?

options.A: Resistance offered by peripheral capillary beds
options.B: Total volume of blood pumped per minute by the heart
options.C: Peak pressure generated during ventricular contraction
options.D: Pressure in the arteries during ventricular relaxation

explanation: Diastolic is the resting pressure. It's what's left in the pipes when the heart muscle relaxes between beats (the bottom number). [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: Where is the normal location to find the apex beat (point of maximal impulse) in a healthy adult?

options.A: Epigastric region just below the xiphoid process
options.B: Left fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line
options.C: Left third intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
options.D: Right fourth intercostal space at the sternal border

explanation: Memorize this landmark! The normal apex beat is found on the left side, at the fifth intercostal space right along the midclavicular line. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h6)

question: What mechanical action of the heart actually causes the apex beat you feel on the chest?

options.A: The sudden closure of the aortic and pulmonary semilunar valves
options.B: The electrical depolarization sweeping across the sinoatrial node
options.C: The passive filling of blood into the right and left atria
options.D: The contraction and twisting of the left ventricle in early systole

explanation: As the left ventricle squeezes and twists at the start of a beat, its tip (apex) taps lightly against the inside of the chest wall. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h6)

question: Which patient position makes it easier to find a hard-to-locate apex beat?

options.A: Trendelenburg position flat on the back

explanation: Rolling the patient slightly onto their left side lets gravity pull the heart closer to the chest wall so you can feel the apex beat much clearer. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the normal size (diameter) of the apex beat impulse in a healthy adult?
explanation: A normal apex beat is quite compact—usually about the size of a coin (1 to 2 cm). If it's much larger, it can be a sign of an enlarged heart. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: Why does long-term high blood pressure (hypertension) cause the apex beat to shift away from its normal spot?

options.A: It weakens the right atrium, shifting the mediastinum upward
options.B: It destroys chest wall cartilage and collapses the intercostal spaces
options.C: It reduces overall blood volume, causing cardiac shrinkage
options.D: It causes left ventricular hypertrophy, enlarging the heart muscle

explanation: When the heart has to pump against high pressure all the time, its muscle thickens (hypertrophy). This makes the heart bigger, moving the apex beat further to the left. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: Which combination of vital signs is a classic warning sign of early shock from blood loss (hypovolemic shock)?

options.B: Hypertension, bradycardia, and deep regular breathing
options.C: Hypotension, tachycardia, and weak thready pulse
options.D: Normal blood pressure, bradypnea, and bounding pulse

explanation: When blood volume drops, blood pressure falls (hypotension). To make up for it, the heart races (tachycardia) and feels weak and thready. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: Why is looking at vital sign trends over time better than just reading one isolated number?

options.A: Trends reveal subtle physiological deterioration or improvement over time
options.B: Hospital administrative policies require multiple entries before diagnosis
options.C: Single readings are always inaccurate due to faulty equipment calibration
options.D: Physicians ignore single vital sign values during daily ward rounds

explanation: A single number only tells you right now. Tracking a trend shows you the direction your patient is heading—getting better or getting worse. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h9)

question: What is your immediate professional duty as a nurse if you find critical, dangerous abnormalities in a patient's vital signs?

options.A: Discard the abnormal readings and repeat the procedure an hour later
options.B: Wait until the next scheduled shift change to inform incoming staff
options.C: Promptly report the abnormal findings to the responsible medical officer
options.D: Document the findings in the nursing notes and discharge the patient

explanation: Patient safety comes first! If vitals are dangerously abnormal, you must alert the doctor right away so help can arrive quickly. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h9)
